quotes.text: Every scoring rule is written down and git-committed, with a timestamp, **before** any data is scored; the commit hash is the proof it was frozen.
Across 7 records with a frozen rule (committed before any day-list existed), the most any day reaches is **K = 2**.
We have **not found a new swarm**.
Each rule was committed before scoring and measured against ordinary-day controls. Two records carry a swarm; the rest are nulls.
A finding is a measurement that matches independently reported events and that a second method reproduces.
A scanner report records the request and when it was made, not what program sent it, and the harness hosts also have ordinary users.
Submitter addresses are replaced by a short code on reading, using a random key that is destroyed after each run.
The pages show counts only: no report contents, links, names or addresses.
